fb.title: FB Case 1: Acute Foreign Body Aspiration in an Adult

patient.name: Mr. Arjun Kumar
patient.chiefComplaint: Sudden choking and noisy breathing for 20 mins
patient.hopi: Developed sudden coughing, difficulty breathing, and stridor while eating peanuts. Unable to speak properly.
patient.pastHistory: No asthma or previous airway issues.

examination.text: Anxious, severe respiratory distress.
No visible FB in oral cavity; inspiratory stridor present. Hoarse voice.
Markedly increased work of breathing with intercostal retractions.

investigations.name: Flexible Laryngoscopy
investigations.summary: No foreign body visualised in accessible upper airway.
investigations.impression: Lower/inaccessible airway foreign body cannot be excluded.

investigations.name: Chest X-ray (PA view)
investigations.summary: Normal or shows mild unilateral air trapping.
investigations.impression: Normal chest radiograph does not rule out radiolucent foreign body aspiration.

investigations.name: Emergency Rigid Bronchoscopy
investigations.summary: Direct visualisation of peanut fragment in tracheobronchial tree.
investigations.impression: Confirms diagnosis and allows immediate optical forceps extraction.

mcq.question: A 35-year-old patient develops sudden choking and respiratory distress while eating peanuts. What is the most definitive provisional diagnosis?
mcq.explanation: Sudden choking during eating followed by stridor and severe hypoxia indicates foreign body aspiration.

management.text: Immediate airway assessment and oxygenation
Age-appropriate choking first-aid / Heimlich maneuver if complete obstruction
Urgent rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia
Blind finger sweep of the pharynx
Delaying airway intervention for routine neck CT scan

fb.managementExplanation: Airway stabilization and urgent bronchoscopic extraction are paramount. Blind finger sweeps can impact a foreign body into the glottis.

fb.title: FB Case 2: Peanut Aspiration in a Young Child

patient.name: Master Kavin Raj
patient.chiefComplaint: Persistent coughing for 1 hour after eating peanuts
patient.hopi: Child was eating peanuts when he experienced sudden choking and cough. Noisy breathing and wheezing followed.

examination.text: Agitated child with persistent paroxysmal cough.
Oral cavity clear. No swelling in tonsils or pharynx.
Decreased breath sounds over right hemithorax with localized expiratory wheeze.

investigations.name: Inspiratory / Expiratory Chest Radiographs
investigations.summary: Unilateral hyperinflation, localized air trapping and mediastinal shift away from right lung.
investigations.impression: Obstructive ball-valve emphysema from right bronchial foreign body.

investigations.name: Pediatric Rigid Bronchoscopy
investigations.summary: Swollen peanut lodge in right main bronchus.
investigations.impression: Direct visualization and extraction with optical forceps.

mcq.question: A 3-year-old child develops persistent coughing and unilateral wheezing immediately after eating peanuts. Most likely diagnosis?
mcq.explanation: Classical triad of paroxysmal cough, wheeze, and unilateral decreased air entry after peanut ingestion points to foreign body aspiration.

management.text: Keep child calm with parents; avoid agitation
Urgent pediatric rigid bronchoscopy under GA
Humidified supplemental oxygen titrated to SpO2
Blind digital throat sweeps
Prescribing bronchodilators and discharging home

fb.managementExplanation: Rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia is the gold standard for extraction in children. Avoid blind sweeping.

fb.title: FB Case 3: Laryngeal Foreign Body Causing Acute Stridor

patient.name: Mr. Sanjay Mohan
patient.chiefComplaint: Sudden choking and aphonia while eating fish
patient.hopi: While eating fish curry, sudden sharp choking occurred with immediate loss of normal voice, severe inspiratory stridor, and air hunger.

examination.text: Patient in tripod position, grasping neck, severe distress.
Inspiratory stridor; voice hoarse and muffled. Marked suprasternal notch indrawing.
Unable to tolerate supine positioning.

investigations.name: Emergency Flexible Nasolaryngoscopy
investigations.summary: Sharp bone fragment wedged across vocal cords and anterior commissure.
investigations.impression: Laryngeal foreign body impaction with subtotal glottic occlusion.

investigations.name: Soft Tissue Neck X-Ray Lateral View
investigations.summary: Linear radiopacity projected over the glottis at C4-C5 level.
investigations.impression: Radiopaque laryngeal foreign body.

mcq.question: Sudden choking, loss of normal voice, and severe inspiratory stridor after eating food containing bones suggest which diagnosis?
mcq.explanation: Acute onset of stridor and aphonia/dysphonia immediately following ingestion indicates obstruction at the level of the larynx.

management.text: Emergency ENT and airway anesthesia intervention
Direct laryngoscopy and controlled forceps removal under GA
Tracheostomy set kept ready at bedside
Blind pharyngeal/laryngeal instrumentation
Delaying airway management for IV contrast CT neck

fb.managementExplanation: Immediate controlled endoscopic removal with a surgical airway (tracheostomy) standby is required. Blind attempts may convert subtotal obstruction into fatal total occlusion.

fb.title: FB Case 4: Tracheal Foreign Body Aspiration

patient.name: Mr. Vignesh Anand
patient.chiefComplaint: Cough and central noisy breathing after food aspiration
patient.hopi: Inhaled a piece of hard candy. Experienced paroxysms of coughing and feels an object moving inside the windpipe with respiration.

examination.text: Frequent coughing paroxysms, audible central rattle.
Audible thud and palpatory thud over the trachea on expiration.
Bilateral equal breath sounds without focal wheezing.

investigations.name: Chest & Neck Radiograph
investigations.summary: Tracheal lucency irregularity; no lobar atelectasis.
investigations.impression: Mobile tracheal foreign body.

investigations.name: Rigid Tracheobronchoscopy
investigations.summary: Smooth foreign body moving freely between carina and subglottis.
investigations.impression: Freely mobile tracheal foreign body requiring immediate grasp and removal.

mcq.question: Audible thud, palpatory thud, and asthmatoid wheeze following a choking episode indicate what diagnosis?
mcq.explanation: The classic triad of audible slap/thud, palpatory thud, and asthmatoid wheeze is pathognomonic of a mobile foreign body in the trachea.

management.text: Immediate rigid bronchoscopy and optical forceps extraction
Maintain upright position and high-flow oxygen
Continuous pulse oximetry and ECG monitoring
Vigorous back blows in a stable conscious patient (risks subglottic impaction)
Postponing intervention overnight because chest X-ray appears unremarkable

fb.managementExplanation: A mobile tracheal foreign body can impact into the subglottis during coughing, causing fatal complete asphyxia. Urgent bronchoscopy is mandatory.

fb.title: FB Case 5: Right Main Bronchus Foreign Body

patient.name: Mr. Pradeep Selvam
patient.chiefComplaint: Persistent unilateral wheeze and cough for 2 days
patient.hopi: Choked while eating roasted corn 2 days ago. The acute choking passed, but has had intractable right-sided chest tightness, wheezing, and dry cough since.

examination.text: Comfortable at rest, coughs upon deep inspiration.
Decreased breath sounds over right middle and lower zones with localized monophonic wheeze.
Normal pharynx and larynx.

investigations.name: Expiratory Chest X-ray
investigations.summary: Right hemithorax hyperlucency with persistent diaphragm flattening during expiration.
investigations.impression: Unilateral obstructive emphysema secondary to check-valve bronchial obstruction.

investigations.name: HRCT Thorax with Virtual Bronchoscopy
investigations.summary: Intraluminal low-attenuation filling defect in the right bronchus intermedius.
investigations.impression: Impacted bronchial foreign body with post-obstructive air trapping.

mcq.question: A patient develops persistent unilateral monophonic wheeze and cough following an unrecognized choking episode. What is the most likely diagnosis?
mcq.explanation: Unilateral monophonic wheeze after choking indicates a bronchial foreign body. Bilateral wheezing is more typical of asthma.

management.text: Rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia for foreign body retrieval
Pre-operative systemic corticosteroid to diminish mucosal edema
Post-procedure chest physiotherapy and auscultation verification
Empiric inhaler therapy alone assuming new-onset adult asthma
Ignoring unilateral wheeze because standard chest radiograph is reported normal

fb.managementExplanation: A foreign body lodged in the bronchus requires bronchoscopic extraction. Neglected cases lead to bronchiectasis, recurrent pneumonia, and lung abscess.

fb.title: FB Case 6: Foreign Body Aspiration in an Elderly Stroke Patient

patient.name: Mr. Ramasamy Natarajan
patient.chiefComplaint: Cough during feeding and fever for 2 days
patient.hopi: Suffered an ischemic stroke 6 months ago with residual dysphagia. Choked on rice gruel two days ago; now has progressive breathlessness, productive cough, and low-grade fever.

examination.text: Elderly gentleman with wet, gurgly voice.
Impaired gag reflex, bilateral palatal weakness.
Coarse crepitations and reduced air entry over right lung base.

investigations.name: Chest X-Ray PA View
investigations.summary: Consolidation and patchy infiltrates in the right lower lobe apical/basal segments.
investigations.impression: Aspiration pneumonia involving gravity-dependent lung segment.

investigations.name: Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES)
investigations.summary: Laryngeal penetration and tracheal aspiration of saliva and food bolus without cough reflex.
investigations.impression: Silent aspiration due to neurological pharyngolaryngeal dysphagia.

mcq.question: An elderly patient with history of stroke develops fever, coughing during meals, and right basilar consolidation. What is the fundamental underlying diagnosis?
options: Aspiration pneumonia due to swallowing dysfunction
mcq.explanation: Stroke-induced cranial nerve deficits impair pharyngolaryngeal reflexes, predisposing to aspiration of food and secretions into dependent lung zones.

management.text: Keep NPO immediately and insert nasogastric feeding tube
IV broad-spectrum antibiotics covering oral anaerobes and gram-negative bacilli
Flexible bronchoscopic suctioning and clearance of aspirated debris
Formal speech and swallow assessment prior to restarting oral intake
Forcing liquid oral feeds while in supine recumbent position

fb.managementExplanation: NPO status prevents recurrent aspiration, while bronchoscopy clears tracheobronchial debris and IV antibiotics treat pneumonia.

fb.title: FB Case 7: Fish Bone Impaction in the Oropharynx

patient.name: Mr. Karthik Balaji
patient.chiefComplaint: Sharp throat pain and dysphagia for 2 hours after fish meal
patient.hopi: Swallowed fish curry and felt an immediate pricking sensation on the right side of the throat. Pain is sharply aggravated by deglutition. Points with one finger to right upper neck.

examination.text: Alert, sitting upright, pointing to right tonsillar bed.
Tongue depression reveals sharp translucent fish bone protruding from upper pole of right palatine tonsil. No stridor or mucosal laceration.

investigations.name: Direct Pharyngeal Illumination
investigations.summary: Fine, sharp translucent bone embedded in the crypt of the right palatine tonsil.
investigations.impression: Visualised accessible oropharyngeal foreign body.

investigations.name: Flexible Nasolaryngoscopy
investigations.summary: Base of tongue, vallecula, and pyriform fossae clear of residual fragments.
investigations.impression: Confirms isolated single foreign body.

mcq.question: Acute sharp pricking throat pain during a meal, strictly localized by the patient with finger-pointing, most likely indicates?
mcq.explanation: Sudden localized sticking sensation exacerbated by swallowing after eating fish is classic for fish bone impaction, commonly at the tonsillar crypts or lingual tonsil.

management.text: Extraction under direct illumination using Tilley or Hartmann forceps
Apply topical lidocaine spray to oropharynx to suppress gagging
Examine base of tongue and vallecula to exclude occult secondary bones
Swallowing large dry food boluses (e.g. bread, bananas) to push the bone down
Blind sweeping with unguided gloved finger

fb.managementExplanation: Direct extraction under clear lighting avoids pushing sharp bones into deeper musculature. Swallowing bread boluses can drive sharp bones transmucosally, risking deep neck space infection.

fb.title: FB Case 8: Nasal Foreign Body with Aspiration Risk

patient.name: Master Adithya Kumar
patient.chiefComplaint: Plastic bead pushed into right nostril with sudden cough
patient.hopi: Mother observed the child insert a round plastic toy bead into the right nostril. While attempting extraction with hairpins at home, child cried, choked suddenly, and began coughing intermittently.

examination.text: Right nasal cavity contains edema and blood; round bead seen initially has slipped posteriorly beyond inferior turbinate.
Intermittent coughing with audible inspiratory airway noise.

investigations.name: Diagnostic Nasal Endoscopy
investigations.summary: Bead has dislodged into nasopharynx hovering near the laryngeal inlet.
investigations.impression: Dislodged foreign body at high risk of immediate laryngeal aspiration.

investigations.name: Neck & Chest Radiograph
investigations.summary: No radiopaque shadow seen (radiolucent toy bead).
investigations.impression: Negative radiograph does not exclude plastic object.

mcq.question: A pediatric nasal foreign body that disappears posteriorly accompanied by sudden choking and tachypnea must immediately be treated as?
mcq.explanation: Inadvertent posterior displacement of a nasal foreign body can cause aspiration into the larynx and tracheobronchial tree, an airway emergency.

management.text: Keep child calm in sitting position; avoid agitation
Emergency rigid endoscopy in operating theatre with airway secured
Use Mother’s Kiss technique or balloon catheter ONLY if object is visible anteriorly in stable child
Blind attempts with unbent forceps pushing the object deeper
Sedating child in emergency room without securing the airway

fb.managementExplanation: Objects dislodged posteriorly can cause fatal airway obstruction. Controlled endoscopic removal with airway equipment ready is required.

fb.title: FB Case 9: Esophageal Button Battery Impaction in a Toddler

patient.name: Baby Ananya
patient.chiefComplaint: Acute refusal of feeds, drooling, and dysphagia for 3 hours
patient.hopi: Child was found playing with a remote control. Subsequently developed irritability, total refusal of oral intake, drooling of saliva, and chest discomfort.

examination.text: Distressed, drooling saliva continuously, refusing all swallows.
No stridor; bilateral vesicular breath sounds.
Fullness and tenderness over lower anterior cervical region.

investigations.name: Neck and Chest X-ray (AP & Lateral)
investigations.summary: Radiopaque circular discoid body at C6 level showing pathognomonic "Double-Ring" (halo) sign on AP and "Step-Off" bevel on lateral.
investigations.impression: Impacted button/disc battery in upper esophagus requiring emergent retrieval within 2 hours.

investigations.name: Rigid Esophagoscopy
investigations.summary: Black liquefactive mucosal necrosis observed surrounding the negative pole of the battery.
investigations.impression: Alkaline liquefaction necrosis of esophageal wall.

mcq.question: An AP radiograph showing a radiopaque circular object with a distinct double-ring (halo) sign in the upper esophagus indicates which true medical emergency?
mcq.explanation: The double-ring sign differentiates a button battery from a coin. Button batteries cause transmural liquefactive necrosis and perforation within 2 hours.

management.text: Immediate emergency rigid esophagoscopy removal within 2 hours
Oral honey administration (if >1 yr old) while arranging transport to mitigate mucosal burn
Keep strictly NPO and establish IV access
Watchful waiting for spontaneous passage into stomach
Inducing emesis with ipecac syrup or saline

fb.managementExplanation: Electrical discharge from an impacted disc battery creates hydroxide ions, causing rapid liquefactive necrosis, tracheoesophageal fistula, or aortic blowout. Emergent endoscopic removal is mandatory.

fb.title: FB Case 10: Sharp Denture Plate Impacted in the Upper Esophagus

patient.name: Mr. Devanand
patient.chiefComplaint: Severe retrosternal pain and inability to swallow saliva
patient.hopi: Accidentally swallowed an old, loose partial acrylic denture with metallic wire clasps during dinner. Immediate retrosternal stabbing pain and total dysphagia.

examination.text: Spitting saliva into kidney dish; grimacing with neck motion.
Tender lower left neck; surgical emphysema (crepitus) palpated over left supraclavicular fossa.

investigations.name: Lateral Neck Soft Tissue X-Ray
investigations.summary: Increased prevertebral soft tissue shadow (>14mm at C6), air in retrovisceral space, and metallic clasp shadow.
investigations.impression: Upper esophageal perforation with cervical surgical emphysema.

investigations.name: CT Neck & Thorax with Oral Non-Ionic Water-Soluble Contrast
investigations.summary: Denture impacted at cricopharyngeal sphincter with transmural breach and extraluminal gas tracks.
investigations.impression: Esophageal perforation with impending superior mediastinitis.

mcq.question: A patient with an impacted sharp denture in the esophagus develops surgical emphysema (crepitus) in the neck. What complication has occurred?
mcq.explanation: Subcutaneous surgical emphysema and prevertebral soft tissue widening following sharp foreign body impaction are signs of esophageal perforation.

management.text: Immediate NPO status, IV broad-spectrum antibiotics, and IV fluids
Urgent ENT / Thoracic surgical exploration and rigid esophagoscopy / cervical esophagotomy
Screening for mediastinitis and abscess formation
Performing a barium swallow study (risk of fatal chemical mediastinitis)
Encouraging patient to eat bread to dislodge the denture

fb.managementExplanation: Perforation requires surgical consultation, NPO status, and IV antibiotics. Water-soluble contrast (Gastrografin) is preferred over barium because barium causes mediastinal granulomatosis.

fb.title: FB Case 11: Café Coronary (Hypopharyngeal Meat Bolus Asphyxia)

patient.name: Mr. Robert Lewis
patient.chiefComplaint: Sudden collapse at a restaurant with cyanosis and aphonia
patient.hopi: While intoxicated at a steakhouse, suddenly stopped speaking, clutched his neck (universal choking sign), became cyanotic, and collapsed unconscious.

examination.text: Unresponsive, central cyanosis, absent spontaneous respirations, pulse thready.
Massive poorly chewed meat bolus wedged across hypopharynx completely occluding laryngeal inlet.

investigations.name: Emergency Direct Laryngoscopy
investigations.summary: Massive steak bolus completely obstructing the supraglottis and vocal cords.
investigations.impression: Complete acute laryngeal inlet mechanical occlusion (Café Coronary).

mcq.question: An intoxicated adult with poor dentition collapses aphonic and cyanotic while eating beef. What is this clinical entity?
mcq.explanation: Café coronary describes fatal upper airway occlusion by a large unchewed meat bolus impacting the hypopharynx, often mistaken for an acute MI.

management.text: Immediate Magill forceps clearance under direct laryngoscopy
Perform immediate abdominal thrusts / Heimlich maneuvers if conscious or basic CPR with direct suction/removal if unconscious
Emergency cricothyroidotomy if oral extraction is blocked
Treating presumptively as myocardial infarction with sublingual nitrates and chest compressions without inspecting the airway
Attempting blind endotracheal tube insertion over the meat bolus

fb.managementExplanation: Immediate removal of the bolus with Magill forceps under direct laryngoscopy or Heimlich maneuvers is life-saving. Blind intubation can push the bolus deeper into the subglottis.

fb.title: FB Case 12: Inhaled Sewing Needle in the Left Basilar Bronchus

patient.name: Ms. Fatima Sana
patient.chiefComplaint: Accidental inhalation of a scarf pin / sewing needle 4 hours ago
patient.hopi: Held a sewing needle between her lips while adjusting her hijab. Sighed deeply and inhaled the needle. Mild transient coughing occurred; she is currently asymptomatic.

examination.text: Comfortable, speaking in full sentences.
Bilateral vesicular breath sounds, no wheeze or crepitations.

investigations.name: Chest X-Ray PA & Lateral
investigations.summary: Slender metallic radiopaque linear object (3 cm) in the left lower lobe posterior basal bronchus.
investigations.impression: Metallic sharp foreign body in bronchial tree.

investigations.name: Flexible & Rigid Bronchoscopy
investigations.summary: Metallic needle tip visible in basilar subsegmental bronchus.
investigations.impression: Foreign body successfully captured with optical grasping forceps.

mcq.question: A young tailor holds a pin in her lips and inhales it during speech, currently displaying no respiratory distress. What is the mandatory next step?
mcq.explanation: Asymptomatic periods are common after sharp foreign body aspiration. Pins can migrate, cause parenchymal laceration, and require urgent bronchoscopy.

management.text: Stat PA and lateral chest radiography
Keep NPO and arrange rigid/flexible bronchoscopy extraction
Fluoroscopic guidance in the operating theatre if deeply lodged
Encouraging forceful coughing fits (risks vascular puncture)
Discharging patient with reassurance because breath sounds are normal

fb.managementExplanation: Sharp metallic pins can penetrate bronchial walls and lacerate adjacent pulmonary vessels. Extraction must be organized without delay.

fb.title: FB Case 13: Inhaled Tooth Fragment Following Maxillofacial Trauma

patient.name: Mr. Balan Chetty
patient.chiefComplaint: Cough and right-sided pleuritic chest pain after road accident
patient.hopi: Involved in a two-wheeler accident 2 days ago suffering facial trauma and loss of anterior incisors. Developed progressive right-sided cough and foul-smelling sputum.

examination.text: Fractured right central incisor with missing tooth crown.
Dullness to percussion and bronchial breathing over right middle zone.

investigations.name: Chest Radiograph (PA View)
investigations.summary: High-density radiopaque tooth-shaped shadow in right intermediate bronchus with distal consolidation.
investigations.impression: Aspirated tooth crown causing secondary post-obstructive pneumonitis.

investigations.name: Thoracic CT with 3D Reconstruction
investigations.summary: Calcified tooth fragment impacted within right bronchus intermedius.
investigations.impression: Obstructing dental foreign body.

mcq.question: Following facial trauma with fractured teeth, a patient develops fever and right lung consolidation. What diagnosis must be investigated?
mcq.explanation: Avulsed or fractured teeth in facial trauma can be aspirated silently into the tracheobronchial tree, causing obstruction and secondary infection.

management.text: Rigid bronchoscopy and extraction using optical forceps
IV broad-spectrum antibiotics for post-obstructive pneumonia
Dental / Maxillofacial review for definitive arch repair
Assuming missing teeth were completely swallowed without chest imaging
Discharging on oral cough syrups

fb.managementExplanation: Missing teeth after facial trauma must be accounted for radiologically. Aspiration requires bronchoscopic clearance to resolve post-obstructive infection.

fb.title: FB Case 14: Live Insect in External Auditory Canal

patient.name: Master Dinesh
patient.chiefComplaint: Severe left ear agony and frantic buzzing sound for 1 hour
patient.hopi: Woke up suddenly with excruciating left ear pain, fluttering, and scratching sounds after a live cockroach entered his ear canal while sleeping on the floor.

examination.text: Live brown insect actively thrashing its legs against the bony external auditory meatus and tympanic membrane. Canal wall hyperemic.

investigations.name: High-Definition Video Otoscopy
investigations.summary: Live organic foreign body (cockroach) abutting the tympanic membrane.
investigations.impression: Active live organic aural foreign body.

mcq.question: What is the absolute first-line step in managing a live insect moving inside the external auditory canal?
options: Instillation of Mineral Oil / 2% Lidocaine to Suffocate the Insect
mcq.explanation: A live insect must be drowned and immobilized with mineral oil or 2% lidocaine before extraction. Attempting to grasp a live insect causes frantic movement and tympanic membrane laceration.

management.text: Immediate instillation of mineral oil, olive oil, or 2% topical lidocaine
Gentle removal with micro-forceps or suction under direct microscope visualization once dead
Inspection of tympanic membrane for perforation after removal
Blind grasping with forceps while the insect is alive and moving
Syringing hygroscopic vegetable foreign bodies with water

fb.managementExplanation: Killing the insect with oil or lidocaine stops excruciating pain and prevents traumatic tympanic perforation during extraction.

fb.title: FB Case 15: Retained Metallic Whistle with Bronchiectasis

patient.name: Master Surya
patient.chiefComplaint: Chronic cough, foul sputum, and recurrent right pneumonia for 6 months
patient.hopi: History of an untreated choking spell 6 months ago while playing with a plastic whistle. Has had continuous productive cough and wheeze treated unsuccessfully as refractory asthma.
patient.pastHistory: Multiple hospitalizations for right lower lobe pneumonia.

examination.text: Clubbing Grade 1. Right lower zone shows bronchial breathing, coarse leathery crackles, and absent air entry at the base.

investigations.name: High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) Chest
investigations.summary: Cylindrical and saccular bronchiectasis with surrounding granulation tissue surrounding an intraluminal foreign body in right basilar bronchus.
investigations.impression: Chronic retained foreign body with secondary irreversible bronchiectasis.

investigations.name: Rigid Bronchoscopy
investigations.summary: Massive hypervascular granulation tissue occluding the right basal trunk; metallic whistle core visible within.
investigations.impression: Foreign body embedded in inflammatory granulation.

mcq.question: Long-standing, neglected retention of a bronchial foreign body typically results in which chronic pulmonary pathology?
mcq.explanation: Prolonged retention of an airway foreign body produces chronic suppuration, fibrous granulation, and bronchiectasis.

management.text: Rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia with granulation debridement
Course of IV antibiotics guided by bronchial aspirate culture
Postural drainage and respiratory rehabilitation
Thoracic surgical lobectomy evaluation if bronchiectasis is irreversible
Continuing empiric asthma therapies without investigating refractory symptoms

fb.managementExplanation: Long-standing foreign bodies become surrounded by granulations. Controlled bronchoscopic extraction is necessary; irreversible damage may require surgical resection.

fb.title: FB Case 16: Expanding Hygroscopic Seed in Pediatric Trachea

patient.name: Master Varun
patient.chiefComplaint: Progressive respiratory distress following watermelon seed aspiration
patient.hopi: Child choked on watermelon seeds 18 hours ago. Symptoms subsided initially but have returned with worsening stridor, air hunger, and retractions as the seed hydrated and swelled.

examination.text: Severe biphasic stridor, suprasternal, intercostal, and epigastric indrawing.
Markedly diminished air entry bilaterally with generalized rhonchi.

investigations.name: AP Soft Tissue Neck & Chest
investigations.summary: Overinflated lungs with bilateral air trapping and subglottic tracheal shadow narrowing.
investigations.impression: Tracheal obstruction from vegetative hygroscopic seed.

investigations.name: Emergency Pediatric Rigid Bronchoscopy
investigations.summary: Watermelon seed swollen to twice its normal size occluding 90% of mid-tracheal lumen.
investigations.impression: Hygroscopic expansion of vegetative organic foreign body.

mcq.question: Why do vegetative foreign bodies (beans, seeds) represent an escalating danger over hours following aspiration?
options: Hygroscopic Absorption of Moisture Causes Expansion and Edema
mcq.explanation: Vegetative matter is hygroscopic; it absorbs water from airway secretions, swells in size, and releases fatty acids causing chemical bronchitis and worsening obstruction.

management.text: Immediate emergency rigid bronchoscopy under GA
Humidified oxygen with head elevated and monitoring in ICU
IV Dexamethasone to combat severe subglottic/tracheal mucosal edema
Delaying extraction until next day elective operating schedule
Chest physiotherapy / postural drainage (risks seed displacement into glottis)

fb.managementExplanation: Expanding vegetative seeds transform partial airway narrowing into complete asphyxia. Emergent rigid bronchoscopy is life-saving.

fb.title: FB Case 17: Battery Ingestion with Tracheoesophageal Fistula

patient.name: Baby Ritika
patient.chiefComplaint: Paroxysms of severe coughing and cyanosis on attempting oral feeds
patient.hopi: Button battery unwitnessed ingestion 4 days ago. Child now chokes and turns blue whenever offered milk or water. Low-grade fever and wheezing have developed.

examination.text: Bilateral diffuse crackles; severe coughing whenever swallowing saliva.
Tracheal tug, subcostal retractions present.

investigations.name: Thoracic CT with 3D Airway & Esophageal Reconstruction
investigations.summary: Transmural necrosis of anterior esophageal and posterior tracheal wall with a 1.2 cm fistulous communication at T2 level.
investigations.impression: Acquired tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF) secondary to button battery necrosis.

investigations.name: Combined Broncho-Esophagoscopy
investigations.summary: Ulcerated fistula between posterior membranous trachea and esophagus.
investigations.impression: Patent corrosive tracheoesophageal fistula.

mcq.question: Coughing and cyanosis during liquid feeds several days after button battery ingestion are characteristic of which severe complication?
mcq.explanation: Electrochemical hydrolysis from button batteries erodes through the esophagus into the trachea, establishing an acquired tracheoesophageal fistula.

management.text: Stop all oral feeds and establish gastrostomy / jejunostomy nutrition
Endotracheal intubation with cuff positioned distal to fistula if ventilatory support is required
Multidisciplinary pediatric surgical and ENT repair
Giving oral contrast or thin fluids to test swallow integrity
Blind nasogastric tube insertion (can pass through fistula into bronchus)

fb.managementExplanation: Acquired TEF requires bypassing the esophagus, isolating the airway from gastric secretions, and planned surgical fistula division and repair.

fb.title: FB Case 18: Subglottic Foreign Body (Eggshell Fragment) in an Infant

patient.name: Master Tanmay
patient.chiefComplaint: Biphasic stridor and hoarse cry for 6 hours
patient.hopi: Choked while eating boiled egg. Succeeded by persistent hoarse cry, severe biphasic stridor, and intercostal indrawing.

examination.text: Agitated infant with inspiratory and expiratory stridor (biphasic).
No visible pharyngeal pathology. Hoarse cry proves laryngeal/subglottic localization.

investigations.name: High-Kilovoltage AP and Lateral Airway Neck Radiograph
investigations.summary: Irregular sharp calcified laminar opacity wedged within the immediate subglottic space.
investigations.impression: Subglottic sharp foreign body.

investigations.name: Direct Laryngoscopy under Inhalational GA
investigations.summary: Curved eggshell fragment wedged sagittally in the subglottis below true cords.
investigations.impression: Direct visualization and careful optical forceps extraction.

mcq.question: Biphasic stridor accompanied by hoarseness in a 10-month-old infant immediately following eating localized the lesion to which anatomical compartment?
mcq.explanation: Biphasic stridor indicates fixed upper airway narrowing at the glottic or subglottic zone.

management.text: Direct laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy under spontaneous ventilation GA
Gentle removal with optical pediatric foreign body forceps
Post-procedure nebulized budesonide / systemic dexamethasone
Blind finger sweep in subglottic space
Forceful blind endotracheal tube intubation (risks pushing shell down into bronchus)

fb.managementExplanation: Controlled removal under spontaneous ventilation anesthesia prevents pushing the foreign body down the trachea.

fb.title: FB Case 19: Fractured Tracheostomy Tube Migration into Bronchus

patient.name: Mr. Chandran
patient.chiefComplaint: Sudden cough, hemoptysis, and missing inner tracheostomy tube flange
patient.hopi: Long-term tracheostomy user wearing an old silver metallic Jackson/Chevalier tube. While cleaning, the tube fractured at the junction of the cannula and neck plate, slipping into the trachea.

examination.text: Only the broken outer flange rests against the anterior neck; the curved distal metallic shaft has disappeared down the stoma.
Unilateral absent breath sounds over right lung.

investigations.name: Emergency Portable Chest Radiograph
investigations.summary: Metallic radiopaque hollow cylinder lodged in the right main bronchus.
investigations.impression: Fractured tracheostomy cannula migrated into right bronchial tree.
